concurrency_primitives: goroutines, buffered channels (cap 256) as bounded job queues, per-worker private maps merged by collector, sync.WaitGroup (join.go), sync.Once (service_data.go) for single 311 load; 4 workers per file, both files ingested concurrently
design_patterns: none named; de facto pipeline/worker-pool fan-out/fan-in; flat main package with one file per question
questions: Which neighborhoods have the most vacant-building notices, and how many 311 requests do they have?
Do neighborhoods with more notices tend to have more 311 requests? (Pearson r)
Among the top-10 notice neighborhoods, where are illegal-dumping requests concentrated?
How does the unresolved-request percentage compare between <100-notice and >=100-notice neighborhoods?
How do average recorded closure times compare between those groups?
overview: Flat single-package Go program (7 files) plus a separate visualize program that renders report.html by re-parsing the engine's printed text. Ingestion uses a reader goroutine feeding 4 aggregating workers per file over bounded channels, with both files loaded concurrently and only per-neighborhood summaries retained (13 MB RSS for 380 MB input). Code is clean and idiomatic with careful data-quality counters, but there are no packages, interfaces, tests, or named design patterns, and the text-scraping visualizer is brittle.
stakeholder_value: All five questions join vacant notices to 311 requests by neighborhood and are addressed to Housing, Public Works, Planning and the Mayor's Office; the dumping-in-vacant-neighborhoods ranking and the finding that high-vacancy areas do not see slower 311 service are actionable. However Q1 is plain counting, Q4/Q5 collapse 213 neighborhoods into two arbitrary buckets using means on skewed data, and nothing is population-normalized, so insight is modest.
issues: No unit tests and no run script; go.mod pins go 1.27.2 which forces a toolchain download
Join stage is token concurrency (4 goroutines intersecting ~290 names); Q2-Q5 analyses run sequentially
visualize/main.go parses human-readable results.txt by string prefix instead of structured data
Q5 uses arithmetic means on heavy-tailed closure times; Q4/Q5 use a coarse two-bucket split
No design pattern named or realized; question orchestration lives inside Q1's reportTopNotices
rationale: Full marks for build, real bundled data, memory discipline and a clean end-to-end run that matches the baseline under the race detector. Concurrency is genuine for ingestion/aggregation but not for join or analysis (11/15). Architecture is organized but single-package with no tests or patterns (8/15), and the five questions are cross-dataset yet partly shallow (11/15). Total 84, B.
